items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: And Sarah Vaughan, she came with the band, and I started to writing music for her.

ctx.x: Hotel, 125th and 7th Avenue. So Billy Eckstine ran up to the room and got me. He says, hey, man. He said, I just heard a little chick that can sing like a mocking bird. He said, look, she's goin' be on the amateur hour tonight, man. He says, you know, we should get Earl to hear this chick, man, and try to get her.

So we said, okay. I say, okay, B, come on. So we went around to Earl Hines' hotel at the Theresa Hotel, and told him, says, come on. I'm taking Billy at his word, because as great as Billy Eckstine is, if he tell me anybody can sing, I gotta believe him. So I helped Billy convince Earl. I says, come on, we're going to amateur night tonight, and we're going to hear this girl sing.

Okay, so we went to amateur night at the Appollo Theater, and here comes her turn, and this girl started to sing, and I'm telling you, right away we convinced Earl he should hire her. We went backstage and talked to this young girl and got her to agree to go with Earl Hines' band. Well, she was sort of shabby and didn't know how to dress or anything. Well, you know, Earl Hines.
